1. # {{projectName}}
2. 
3. Scaffolded with `pantoken-scaffold canvas-theme-editor` (or `pantoken-ai scaffold canvas-theme-editor`)
4. — upload-ready assets for Canvas LMS's **Theme Editor**, plus a local preview for authoring Rich
5. Content Editor (RCE) page templates styled with
6. [`@pantoken/components`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@pantoken/components).
7. 
8. ## What's here
9. 
10. - `theme.css` / `theme.js` — upload these two files under **Theme Editor → Advanced** in Canvas.
11.   They're built for the CDN provider/theme/mode you chose when scaffolding (`--cdn`/`--theme`/
12.   `--theme-mode`; jsDelivr/rebrand/light by default) and include a loader for
13.   `@pantoken/interactions` (wires up component behaviors like modal, tooltip, and drilldown).
14. - `index.html` / `src/main.ts` — a local, TinyMCE-based editor (`npm run dev`) that mirrors Canvas's
15.   RCE so you can author page templates against pantoken's classes before copying them into Canvas.
16.   The page itself is built with pantoken's `wrapper` layout: click **Edit theme** to open a tray
17.   with **Config** / **CSS** / **JS** tabs (CDN provider/theme/mode selects, and syntax-highlighted,
18.   hand-editable copies of `theme.css`/`theme.js` that feed the live preview), and the **?** button
19.   for full instructions. Use the **Layouts** toolbar button to start from one of pantoken's bundled
20.   starter page layouts (hero, callout, two-column, rubric note, testimonial), sourced from
21.   [`@pantoken/plugin-layouts`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@pantoken/plugin-layouts).
22. 
23. ## Develop
24. 
25. ```sh
26. npm install
27. npm run dev
28. ```
29. 
30. This opens a Vite dev server with:
31. 
32. - An **editor** pane (TinyMCE, matching the version/config
33.   [instructure/canvas-lms](https://github.com/instructure/canvas-lms) itself uses — see below).
34.   Use the **Layouts** button to load one of the bundled starter layouts (this replaces the whole
35.   document, after a confirm, rather than inserting at the cursor), and the **Source code** toggle
36.   to hand-edit the raw HTML in a syntax-highlighted (CodeMirror) view alongside the editor, with
37.   the preview pane updating live as you type — unlike TinyMCE's stock `code` plugin, which edits in
38.   a one-shot modal dialog with no live preview.
39. - A **preview** pane showing the editor's content with the current CSS/JS tab's stylesheet/script
40.   applied (not just the resolved CDN URLs), wrapped to match Canvas's own content-area background
41.   and max width — a faithful "what this will look like once uploaded to Canvas" check, updated
42.   live as you type or edit the theme.
43. - The editor and preview panes sit in a split view you can resize by dragging the divider, stack
44.   vertically instead of side by side, and swap the order of (drag a pane's toolbar onto the other,
45.   or use the **Swap panes** button). Each pane has its own fullscreen button.
46. - The **Edit theme** tray's **Config** tab holds the CDN provider/theme/mode selects and
47.   **Download theme.css** / **Download theme.js** links; its **CSS**/**JS** tabs are editable copies
48.   of the generated files — hand-edit them and the preview picks up your changes directly. Changing
49.   a Config select re-generates the CSS/JS tabs unless you've already edited them, in which case a
50.   **Regenerate from config** button appears instead of silently overwriting your edit.
51. 
52. ## Workflow
53. 
54. 1. Upload `theme.css` and `theme.js` to Canvas's Theme Editor (**Advanced → CSS / JavaScript**) so
55.    pantoken's classes are available on every page.
56. 2. Run `npm run dev`, use **Layouts** to start from a bundled starter, and edit it like you
57.    would in Canvas's own RCE.
58. 3. Click **Copy HTML** and paste the result into a Canvas page's RCE (switch to the HTML editor
59.    view first). Canvas sanitizes pasted HTML server-side — this scaffold doesn't attempt to
60.    replicate that, so always verify the pasted result in Canvas (see "Notes on Canvas's RCE"
61.    below).
62. 
63. ## Notes on Canvas's RCE
64. 
65. Canvas's Rich Content Editor runs TinyMCE and sanitizes submitted HTML on the server against an
66. allowlist (`gems/canvas_sanitize` in canvas-lms, kept in sync with TinyMCE's own
67. `valid_elements`/`extended_valid_elements`). What that allowlist means for templates built here:
68. 
69. - `class`, `id`, `style`, `title`, `role`, and `aria-*` attributes are allowed on every element —
70.   pantoken's `class="instui-*"` styling hooks (and inline `style`, e.g. for CSS anchor positioning)
71.   **do** survive being pasted and saved, contrary to older guidance in this file. `<script>` tags
72.   are always stripped.
73. - **RCE-safe pantoken components**: static/display components — alert, view, heading, text, table,
74.   a button-as-`<a>` (not a real `<button>`), blockquote. Stick to semantic HTML pantoken already
75.   supports (`div`, `p`, `span`, `a`, `img`, headings, lists, tables).
76. - **RCE-unsafe**: anything from `@pantoken/interactions`'s behavior set — modal, tooltip,
77.   drilldown, close-button, or any other component driven by the native `popover`/`popovertarget`/
78.   `command`/`commandfor` attributes. Those attributes aren't in Canvas's sanitizer allowlist, so
79.   the markup survives but the interactive behavior silently breaks the first time the page is
80.   saved in Canvas, even with `theme.js`'s `@pantoken/interactions` loader present. Real form
81.   elements (`input`, `form`, `button`, `select`, `textarea`, `label`) and inline `<svg>` are
82.   stripped outright — none of the bundled starter templates use them.
83. 
84. `theme.js` loads `@pantoken/interactions` from the CDN, which runs in Canvas's global page scope —
85. useful for interactions on pages you build directly in Canvas's RCE with raw HTML edits, but (per
86. above) any `popover`/`command`-attribute-driven markup pasted from the RCE preview here won't stay
87. interactive once saved.
